title: Adding a five-year PDO mean raised six-year mean error at 1980-2014 starts and did not explain 2020-2025
abstract: We tested a trailing five-year PDO mean as a repair to a monthly memory and ENSO model for six-year mean PDO. Matched fits used earlier rows from 1960. Across 35 overlapping windows that start in 1980-2014, the added term raised mean squared error from 0.28135 to 0.31975, or 13.65%. Mean continuous ranked probability score rose by 8.76%. Point error also rose in six disjoint windows. The observed 2020-2025 mean was -1.99514. The added model gave an expected mean of -0.284 and a central 95% conditional simulation range of -0.957 to 0.401. None of 3,999 draws was as low as observed. Two- and ten-year mean checks and recent 36-month residual blocks also missed that mean. The result limits this statistical repair; it does not rule out physical memory or show a new climate regime. Known interval selection, overlapping windows, fixed coefficients, revised indices and supplied future ENSO limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, simulation means, source hashes, reproduction instructions, an arithmetic audit and a figure are included. Raw source tables stay external.

display.caption: Earlier six-year mean PDO and recent conditional model ranges. Historical windows overlap. Actual ENSO is supplied during all target periods. Lines show central 95% simulation ranges under fixed coefficients, not calibrated climate confidence intervals.
